column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew leaves the condemning subject implicit; BSB expressly repeats “the LORD.”
Hebrew expressly names the root and says it will not totter; BSB says the righteous cannot be uprooted.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew identifies the counsels as deceit; BSB says they lead to deceit.
Hebrew says “mouth”; BSB uses “speech.”
Hebrew says “they are no more”; BSB has “perish.”
Hebrew describes a person twisted in heart; BSB makes “a twisted mind” the subject.
Hebrew says “bread”; BSB uses the broader “food.”
Hebrew says “knows the soul of his animal”; BSB says “regards the life.” “Only” is not explicit.
Hebrew says “bread” and “lacking heart”; BSB has “food” and “lacks judgment.”
Hebrew says “net” and that the root “gives”; BSB has “plunder” and “flourishes.”
Hebrew retains the images of lips and a snare; BSB expresses this as a man trapped by rebellious speech.
Hebrew speaks of “the fruit of a man’s mouth” and an active returning of the hands’ recompense; BSB makes the work itself return.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew says the prudent man “covers disgrace”; BSB has “overlooks an insult.”
Hebrew uses the image of breathing out faithfulness; BSB says “speaks the truth.”
Hebrew has plural “thrusts of a sword”; BSB has a singular “piercing sword.”
Hebrew has singular “lip”; BSB has plural “lips.”
Hebrew has singular “heart”; BSB has “hearts.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew says “heart of fools,” making the possessors plural; BSB has “a foolish heart.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew describes examining a companion; BSB renders this as being cautious in friendship. “Way” is singular in Hebrew.
Hebrew describes wealth as precious; BSB turns this into an action, “prizes his possession.”
Printed Hebrew has “not death” in the second clause; BSB says another path leads to death.
